A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ATCs are more efficient in managing multiple task-sets, but the training only improves their ability to resolve conflict between task-relevant and task-irrelevant information in a reactive fashion.
the ATCs have a more efficient proactive strategy, which is enhanced by training.
cognitive control is not an innate trait, but it can be enhanced by specific training and that the training itself can modulate the type of cognitive control adopted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the training of ATCs, a highly demanding task that requires a high level of attentional resources, is a suitable model to investigate the effects of experience on cognitive control strategies.

cognitive functions, like executive control and attention, can be shaped by life experiences and that this can be a source of inter-individual variability, which should be taken into account in cognitive science.
